title: Sub-parsec-scale jet-driven water maser with possible gravitational acceleration in the radio galaxy NGC 1052
question: Is the 321-GHz H2O emission in NGC 1052 a maser (brightness temperature, size, variability), and what do its velocity structure, drift and spatial distribution say about the jet-torus region?

what.value: Earlier 2022-05-12 ALMA detection spectrum/components (1333 and 1467 km/s) used for drift comparison

evidence.quote: If B1 is identified as the 1333 km s$^{-1}$ component (cite: 2023PASJ...75L...1K) on 2022-05-12

recipe.method: Standard CASA calibration, smoothed bandpass, continuum subtraction in BB4, self-calibration on target
key_parameters: 9-channel bandpass smoothing; flux 2.104 Jy J0423-0120, 1.304 Jy J0238+1636

recipe.method: Spectra at phase-centre pixel of tclean cubes; nls fit of 7 Gaussian/Lorentzian components

recipe.goal: Measure emission sizes and brightness temperature
recipe.method: Gaussian fit to visibility amplitude vs uv distance for continuum and blue (1360-1500 km/s) and red (1500-1625 km/s) line components
Difmap CLEAN with uniform weighting on BB1-3; compare self-cal agreement factors with single vs aligned components

recipe.goal: Position line components and velocity gradient
recipe.method: uvmodelfit point-source fits on continuum-subtracted visibilities binned by 5 channels (4.57 km/s); linear regression V_LSR ~ jJ + dD
key_parameters: detection threshold 3x line image rms; J axis PA=68.35 deg

recipe.goal: Derive drift, acceleration and maser distance
recipe.method: Velocity change of B1 over 14 days gives g; r = sqrt(GM/g)
assumptions: M_BH = 1.5e8 Msun; drift due to gravitational acceleration

evidence.quote: The integrated flux densities of $10.79 \pm 0.33$ Jy km s$^{-1}$ and $14.32 \pm 0.43$ Jy km s$^{-1}$
The integrated flux densities of $10.79 \pm 0.33$ Jy km s$^{-1}$ and $14.32 \pm 0.43$ Jy km s$^{-1}$
isotropic luminosities of $1120 \pm 34$ L$_{\Sol}$ and $1486 \pm 45$ L$_{\Sol}$

answer_key.quantity: Blue component peak flux increase in 14 d

evidence.quote: the peak flux density increased by $34.5 \pm 4.2$% and the center velocity shifted by $4.85 \pm 0.5$ km s$^{-1}$ in 14 days
increased from $0.624 \pm 0.019$ Jy to $0.704 \pm 0.021$ Jy by $12.8 \pm 4.2$%
allowed us to constrain the size of emission region in $<0.6$ milliarcsec (mas) and the brightness temperature of $T_{\rm B} > 10^6$ K.
B1 maser component showed the velocity drift of $127 \pm 13$ km s$^{-1}$ yr$^{-1}$ or acceleration of $g = 4.0 \times 10^{-3}$ m s$^{-2}$.
We identified velocity gradient of $-174 \pm 19$ km s$^{-1}$ mas$^{-1}$ along the jet.
The change of weighted mean velocity corresponds to $164 \pm 37$ km s$^{-1}$ yr$^{-1}$
